item.description: Tender Notice - Preparation of the Detailed Technical Specification and the Development of the Software for the Unified Automated Information and Analytical System of the Central Election Commission of Ukraine (Phase I) International IDEA - The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance Tender Reference No: 2026-07-097 Assignment Name: Preparation of the Detailed Technical Specification and the development of the software for the Unified Automated Information and Analytical System of the Central Election Commission of Ukraine (Phase I) Project Name: U-VOTE (Ukrainians Voting: Organizing Trustworthy Elections) Deadline for Submissions: Proposals must be submitted on or before 23:59 (CET), 7 October 2026 . Late submissions will not be considered for evaluation. Address for Submissions: E-mail: tendersubmissions@idea.int This email address is set up with an auto-response to acknowledge emails received. If you do not receive an auto-reply, please send a text message prior to the submission deadline (NO CALLS; CALLS WILL NOT BE ANSWERED) to +46725375735. In your text message, please provide the following: Tender reference no. and title; Email address you used for submission; Date and time you sent your submission (e.g. 01 December 2021, 12:30 CET ); Please also send the above information to tender@idea.int before the deadline for submission. Format for Submissions: Proposal must be submitted by email. Technical and Financial proposals must be submitted in separate files and marked accordingly. Price should not be mentioned in the Technical Proposal. The following text should be put in the subject field of the email: Tender No. (2026-07-097) Technical and Financial Proposals – Do not open before 23:59 (CET), 7 October 2026. Email Address for Clarifications: E-mail: tender@idea.int Clarifications may be requested via e-mail no later than 23 September 2026 at the above email address. Note a response to a request for clarifications will be issued to all tenderers on our website http://www.idea.int/ . Therefore, tenderers are advised to check the website regularly during the process. Note : there are two different email addresses as outlined above, one to be used for Submission of your final proposal and the second one to be used for clarifications and other related correspondence. REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS Section 1 General Information 1.1 The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA) is an intergovernmental organization established in 1995, with member states across all continents, which aims to support sustainable democracy world-wide and assist in the development of institutions and the culture of democracy. At the interface between research, fieldwork and the donor community, IDEA provides a forum for dialogue, builds networks of experts, develops training materials and provides strategic advice at international, regional and national level, cooperating with a range of organizations. 1.2 International IDEA now invites proposals from qualified bidders for the provision of software development services for the Unified Automated Information and Analytical System of the Central Election Commission of Ukraine. A detailed description of the assignment is provided in the Terms of Reference attached to this Request for Proposal. The Framework Agreement resulting from this procurement may, at International IDEA’s discretion, also be used for the development and implementation of subsequent phases of the System. The use of the Framework Agreement for any subsequent phase shall be optional and shall not constitute an obligation on the part of International IDEA to procure such subsequent services from the Framework Agreement holder. 1.3 Tentative timeframe: It is anticipated that the services will commence in October 2026 and will be completed according to the delivery schedule defined in the Terms of Reference (TOR) and agreed in the contract. Section 2 Preparation of Proposals Essential Requirements 2.1 Language: The official language for the proposal, contract, reports and any other documents in relation to the assignment is English. All documents for the CEC, as well as correspondence with the CEC, must also be provided in Ukrainian. 2.2 To be eligible for consideration, the bidder must demonstrate the following experience and capabilities: A. Legal and Organizational Eligibility The Bidder must be a legally registered entity with an established presence in Ukraine and hold all licences, permits, and government approvals required to perform the Services under this solicitation; The Bidder may engage subcontractors for the performance of specific parts of the Services. The total value of the Services to be performed by subcontractors shall not exceed 35% of the total Contract value. Any proposed subcontracting exceeding this threshold shall be clearly identified and justified in the proposal and shall be subject to the prior written approval of International IDEA and the CEC. The Bidder shall clearly identify all proposed subcontractors in its proposal, including the scope of Services and responsibilities assigned to each subcontractor. Each proposed subcontractor shall comply with all applicable legal, licensing, permitting and regulatory requirements relevant to the Services it will perform. Key experts may be provided by proposed subcontractors, provided that this is clearly identified in the proposal and their availability for the assignment is demonstrated. The Bidder shall remain fully responsible for the performance of the Contract, including the performance, acts and omissions of its subcontractors and any key experts provided them. Relevant Experience The Bidder must demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) software development projects of comparable scope, size, and complexity within the last five (5) years preceding the commencement of this procurement procedure. Where a referenced project is subject to confidentiality, security or classification restrictions that prevent the Bidder from providing the evidence listed below, the Bidder may provide alternative verifiable evidence sufficient to demonstrate the nature, scope, complexity and successful completion of the assignment. International IDEA reserves the right to request additional information and/or undertake appropriate verification of such experience; At least one (1) of the referenced projects must have been delivered for a public sector entity. Projects implemented for public sector entities in Ukraine or abroad, including international organizations and donor-funded projects, as well as comparable large-scale, high-security information systems delivered for the private sector (e.g. banking, telecommunications, or critical infrastructure), shall be considered; Compliance with this requirement shall be demonstrated by providing, for each referenced project, one or more of the following: a copy of the relevant contract; a client reference letter; an acceptance certificate (or equivalent evidence of successful completion); or a reference to a publicly available procurement record (e.g. Prozorro). In the case of a consortium or joint venture, the above qualification requirements may be satisfied cumulatively by the consortium members. The experience of declared subcontractors may also be taken into account, provided that the respective subcontractor will perform the relevant part of the Services. Advantage Criteria Experience in developing or modernizing electoral/election-related information systems, or other comparable large-scale, mission-critical public-sector information systems; Experience integrating information systems with Ukrainian state registries and interoperability platforms (e.g. Trembita, State Voter Register, Unified State Register); Demonstrated experience in developing or modernizing high-availability and/or mission critical information systems designed to operate under peak-load and/or unstable connectivity conditions. Capacity Statement The Bidder must demonstrate sufficient financial, technical, and managerial capacity, as well as the necessary facilities and organizational resources, to successfully perform the Services under this procurement; The Bidder's aggregate turnover for the last three (3) completed financial years shall not be less than UAH 50,000,000, supported by appropriate financial documentation. B. Personnel Qualifications and Expertise The Bidder shall propose a qualified multidisciplinary project team with demonstrated experience in software architecture, business analysis, software engineering, quality assurance, cybersecurity, system integration, and project management. The proposed team should include at a minimum, the following key roles: Project Manager; Solution/Software Architect; Business Analyst; Lead Software Developer; Quality Assurance Lead; The Bidder shall additionally demonstrate access to the specialist expertise required for the performance of the Services, including, where applicable, cybersecurity, DevOps/infrastructure, Linux systems engineering, system integration/API development, data architecture, UX/UI and technical documentation. The proposed key experts shall meet the following minimum qualification requirements Key Expert Minimum Qualification and Experience Project Manager At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience, including at least three (3) years of experience managing software development or implementation of projects of comparable scope and complexity. Solution/Software Architect At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience, including at least three (3) years in solution and/or software architecture for complex information systems. Business Analyst At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience, including demonstrated experience in business and requirements analysis for complex information systems. item.title: Vertaler en Conferentietolk (m/v) Moedertaal Nederlands/Traducteur H/F Natif Néerlandais
item.description: Vertaler en Conferentietolk (m/v) Moedertaal Nederlands Eureca Strasbourg, France KLAAR VOOR EEN NIEUWE UITDAGING? De Centrale Commissie voor de Rijnvaart (CCR) heeft sinds 1815 als belangrijkste taak het waarborgen van de veiligheid en de welvaart van de Rijnvaart . Deze internationale organisatie staat bekend om haar belangrijke rol in de binnenvaart en is actief op het snijvlak van technische, sociale en milieuvraagstukken. Het wervingsbureau Eureca zoekt voor deze organisatie een vertaler en conferentietolk (m/v) met Nederlands als moedertaal , ter versterking van het team van vertalers. Functie op basis van een tijdelijk contract (duur: 4 jaar) met zicht op omzetting naar een vast contract. Mooi kantoor in het hart van Straatsburg met de mogelijkheid tot gedeeltelijk thuiswerken . DE FUNCTIE DIE WIJ JE AANBIEDEN Je rapporteert aan de secretaris-generaal en maakt deel uit van het team van vertalers. Jouw taken omvatten: Het vertalen van redactionele, technische en soms politiek gevoelige teksten vanuit het Duits en het Frans naar het Nederlands , met inachtneming van deadlines, kwaliteitseisen en de geldende terminologie, waarbij je je werklast zelfstandig en flexibel indeelt; Het volgen van ontwikkelingen binnen de werkterreinen van de organisatie en van terminologische en taalkundige ontwikkelingen, en het actualiseren van vertaalgeheugens en woordenlijsten; Nauwe samenwerking met de auteurs over taalkundige en stilistische keuzes; Simultaan vertalen van het Duits naar het Nederlands en omgekeerd tijdens vergaderingen, werkgroepen en gesprekken met tolk die plaatsvinden op het hoofdkantoor van de organisatie; Voorbereiding van elke tolkopdracht: bestudering van de werkdocumenten, de agenda en videomateriaal, gericht terminologisch onderzoek. WAT DEZE FUNCTIE AANTREKKELIJK MAAKT Het opbouwen van specialistische expertise op technisch, politiek en sectoraal gebied; Goede begeleiding tijdens je inwerkperiode; Werken in een internationale, dynamische en stimulerende werkomgeving. JE BENT GESCHIKT VOOR DEZE FUNCTIE ALS Je bent afgestudeerd met een master in vertalen en conferentietolken en beheerst naast je moedertaal, het Nederlands, ook het Duits uitstekend. Een goede beheersing van het Frans (B2 – C1) is een pluspunt voor vertalingen naar het Nederlands; Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar ervaring in vertalen en tolken; Je bent georganiseerd, nauwgezet en werkt graag in teamverband. Maar bovenal heb je passie voor kwaliteit! UW VOORDELEN Een contract voor een periode van 4 jaar met de mogelijkheid tot omzetting in een contract voor onbepaalde tijd na afloop van deze 4 jaar; Een belastingvrij nettosalaris; Een goede ziektekosten- en pensioenverzekering; Een werkweek van 38 uur, met de mogelijkheid om 2 dagen per week thuis te werken, en 30 vakantiedagen per jaar. Solliciteer door je cv en motivatiebrief te sturen naar: cbouquet@eureca-rh.com . Traducteur H/F Natif Néerlandais Eureca Strasbourg, France PRÊT(E) POUR UN NOUVEAU DÉFI ? La Commission centrale pour la navigation du Rhin (CCNR) est une organisation internationale de plus de 200 ans dont le siège est à Strasbourg. Elle compte cinq États membres (Allemagne, Belgique, France, Pays-Bas et Suisse) et a pour mission principale d’assurer la sécurité et la prospérité de la navigation rhénane. La CCNR est une organisation à la pointe de l’innovation pour permettre à la flotte rhénane d’être à l’avant-garde et de faire face aux défis d’aujourd’hui: la digitalisation, le verdissement, l’automatisation, l’adaptation au changement climatique, les qualifications du personnel ou encore la position économique du secteur. Au-delà du Rhin, de nombreuses activités de la CCNR sont maintenant réalisées dans un cadre européen. Le cabinet de recrutement Eureca recherche pour cette organisation un Traducteur H/F, de langue maternelle néerlandaise , pour renforcer son équipe linguistique. Poste en CDD (durée de 4 ans) et perspective de transformation en CDI. De beaux locaux en plein cœur de Strasbourg avec possibilité de télétravail partiel . LA MISSION QUE L’ON VOUS PROPOSE Rattaché(e) à la secrétaire générale et au sein de l’équipe de traducteurs, vos missions incluent: (80% du temps) Traduction de l’allemand et du français vers le néerlandais de textes rédactionnels, techniques et parfois politiquement sensibles, dans le respect des délais, des exigences de qualité et de la terminologie en vigueur en organisant votre charge de travail avec autonomie et flexibilité; Veille sur les domaines d'activité de l’organisation ainsi que sur les nouveautés terminologiques et linguistiques et mise à jour des mémoires de traduction et glossaires; Collaboration étroite avec les auteurs sur les choix linguistiques et stylistiques; (20% du temps) Ponctuellement, interprétation simultanée de l’allemand vers le néerlandais et inversement à l’occasion de réunions, groupes de travail et entretiens interprétés se tenant au siège de l’organisation; Préparation de chaque mission d’interprétation: prise de connaissance des documents de travail, de l’ordre du jour, des support vidéo, recherche terminologique ciblée. VOUS AIMEREZ Développer une véritable expertise sectorielle, technique ou politique, au fil des textes; Bénéficier d'un accompagnement lors de votre intégration pour faciliter votre prise de poste; Evoluer dans un environnement de travail international, dynamique et stimulant. VOUS RÉUSSIREZ À CE POSTE SI Diplômé(e) d’un Master en traduction , vous avez une excellente maîtrise de l’allemand en plus de votre langue maternelle, le néerlandais. Une bonne maîtrise du français (B2 – C1) est un atout; Idéalement, vous êtes diplômé(e) d’un Master en interprétation avec l’allemand et le néerlandais comme langues de travail ; Vous bénéficiez d’une expérience de 3 ans minimum en traduction et idéalement en interprétation; Organisé(e), vous êtes rigoureux(se) et vous appréciez le travail en équipe. Mais avant tout, vous avez la passion du travail bien fait! VOS AVANTAGES Un contrat de 4 ans avec une possibilité de conversion en CDI à l’issue de ces 4 années; Une rémunération nette d’impôts; Une bonne couverture santé et prévoyance; Une semaine de travail de 38 heures, 2 jours de télétravail par semaine, 30 jours de congés par an. Postulez en envoyant votre CV et LM à: cbouquet@eureca-rh.com . Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying. Share this Job

item.description: Communications Trainee ChargeUp Europe Brussels, Belgium About ChargeUp Europe ChargeUp Europe is the voice of the electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure industry. EV charging is an innovative, fast-evolving, dynamic sector, at the forefront of the green and digital transition. Our growing membership stands for an EV charging infrastructure roll-out that starts from the consumer needs, makes EV driving convenient across borders, and promotes an open-market model supported by open standards and protocols. Function ChargeUp Europe is looking for a driven, enthusiastic junior professional for the position of Communications Trainee. The trainee will assist the ChargeUp Europe team in all communications activities and projects, including (but not limited to) helping with planning and executing events, supporting the delivery of our communications workplan, and developing content for our social media channels, while servicing members’ needs. This position will offer an opportunity to develop a broad range of communications skills, both through direct experience and by exposure to a network of seasoned communications professionals from the membership. Expected tasks 1. Social media & communications outreach: Creating engaging social media content – both short and long-form – primarily for LinkedIn, ensuring alignment with ChargeUp Europe’s visual identity; Designing clear, meaningful data visualisations and infographics to distil complex information into accessible content; Proactive outreach to stakeholders (e.g. podcast guests and hosts) and support in coordinating activities related to campaigns, podcasts and thematic series; Assisting in drafting written content for social media channels and the ChargeUp Europe website, as well as internal communication tasks and content-creation. 2. Ad-hoc assistance to the Communications Coordinator: Providing administrative and communication support, including document formatting, research, and external communications where needed; Offering ad-hoc assistance in communicating with members and handling day-to-day matters; Collecting, synthesising and analysing information from diverse sources, including data gathering, stakeholder mapping and rapid review of reports to extract key insights. 3. Creative thinking & content development: Contributing fresh, creative ideas to support communications, events and stakeholder engagement; Helping to develop concepts, visuals and messaging for campaigns, events and other formats; Keeping the ChargeUp Europe website up to date; Draft the ChargeUp Europe quarterly newsletter. 4. Logistical support for events: Providing logistical support for online and onsite events (webinars, workshops, presentations), including links, invitations and communication kits. 5. Service to the members: Responding to communications-related requests from ChargeUp Europe members and supporting member-facing activities. Please note that this list is non-exhaustive, and other tasks may be performed under this role. Required skills and competencies Master’s degree in communications or other relevant field; A basic understanding of the European policy landscape and EU institutions; Excellent writing skills in English; Interest in e-mobility; Good interpersonal and organisational skills; Experience in writing for social media, particularly LinkedIn; Experience with Canva. Our offer Targeted start date: asap. Duration: until July 2027. Contract type: CIP (la convention d’immersion professionnelle), full time, based in Brussels (flexible hybrid working regime) Renumeration: per CIP requirements Hiring process Interested candidates should send their application in English by 2 November 2026 COB at the latest to secretariat@chargeupeurope.eu , mentioning “Communications trainee” in the subject line. Please note that interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis: applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as the search will be stopped once a suitable candidate has been identified. The application should include: a CV; a cover letter, not written by AI. The cover should not be a repetition of your resume, but a document of maximum 2 pages covering the 4 questions below: What is your motivation for joining ChargeUp Europe; Tell us about a piece of content you made (post, video, newsletter, flyer…) that didn't land the way you hoped. What do you think went wrong, and what would you change? (Include a link or screenshot.); Find an organization similar to ours that does communications better. Show us one example and explain why it works; Pick one of our Linkedln posts from the 4 weeks. What would you keep, and what would you have done differently? a selection of 3 writing examples, preferably across channels/formats; a canva visual you developed. Please note that ChargeUp Europe will not consider applications that are not complete. ChargeUp Europe values diversity and encourages applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews. Please note that applicants must be authorised to work in the EU. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying. Share this Job

item.description: Internship - Competition Economics BRG Brussels, Belgium As an intern you will be an integral part of our team in our Brussels and Paris offices. You will be involved in real work that has an impact on clients and businesses. You will be working closely with our experts on a variety of cases in the competition space where you will be able to contribute to the analysis. The work of an intern can be both qualitative and quantitative in nature, and projects range from industry and subject matter research to data collection to the preparation of economic, statistical, and other forms of analysis. The ideal candidate will have skills in the following areas: You enjoy working in a team. You are passionate about economics. You like conceptual issues and working with data. You have an interest in competition economics and a good knowledge of theoretical and/or empirical microeconomics and industrial organisation. You can draft and communicate effectively in English. A good knowledge of other languages (e.g., German, French, Spanish, Italian, Polish, etc.) is an asset. You can write simple codes in Stata and/or R that are self-explanatory and easy to follow. You have a positive can-do attitude and you are willing to proactively engage with your colleagues. What you will be doing as an intern: Build expertise through training: From the start, you will benefit from a comprehensive onboarding and training program to equip you with the tools needed for a smooth transition into project work. Tackle real-world problems: Use economic theory and industry insights to help solve complex issues faced by our clients. Work with data that matters: Analyse real client datasets using advanced tools and statistical techniques to extract meaningful insights. Develop rigorous economic models: Construct models based on economic theory and industry-specific considerations to provide clear answers to complex questions. Explore current trends and debates: Conduct research into the latest industry developments and academic literature to support client work and stay ahead of emerging issues. Collaborate in a team setting: Work closely with our team to contribute to project success. Take part in the office’s daily life: Join team-building events, sports sessions, and other social activities that enrich your internship experience. In this key advisory capacity, you will lead and execute targeted advocacy strategies during critical legislative moments within the European Union decision-making framework. You will serve as a core technical and political resource, ensuring EWABA’s positions on critical legislation (including revisions of the REDIV, EU ETS, ReFuelEU Aviation, FuelEU Maritime, and CO₂ Standards for Cars, Vans, and HDVs) are effectively communicated to key decision-makers across the EU Commission, Parliament, and Council. Key Responsibilities Legislative advocacy Institutions outreach: design and execute advocacy campaigns targeting the European Commission, European Parliament (MEPs, APAs, group advisers), and the Council of the EU (Permanent Representations, national ministries); Legislative tracking: monitor and analyse key EU energy, climate, and transport dossiers (revisions of the REDIV, EU ETS, ReFuelEU Aviation, FuelEU Maritime, and CO₂ Standards for Cars, Vans, and HDVs, delegated and implementing legislation and other); Position papers & amendments: contribute to the development of EWABA materials, such as position papers, briefing notes, internal communications and concrete legislative amendment proposals tailored to EU policymakers. Strategic Support and interest representation Executive support: work closely with EWABA’s Government Affairs Director and Secretary General to align advocacy outreach with the association’s overarching strategic priorities; Interest representation: Drafting EU stakeholder consultations, drafting & proposing key deliverables and delivering engagement plans to represent the waste-based and advanced biofuels industry where most effective, such as expert groups, public hearings, and industry platforms; Member engagement: assist in written and verbal briefing of EWABA members on regulatory developments, consensus building, and translating complex EU policy developments into actionable intelligence. Reporting to the EWABA Government Affairs Working Group. Candidate profile Experience Biofuels expertise: minimum 10+ years of dedicated public affairs/government relations experience in EU energy, climate, or transport policy, with specific, deep understanding and expertise in biofuels EU legislation; Proven track record: demonstrated success in influencing policy at EU level including history of positive results in participation in EU legislative processes as an interest representative or decision-maker; EU institutional network: Good relationship builder with an established network of contacts across DG ENER, DG CLIMA, DG MOVE, DG GROW, key MEPs/political group advisors in ENVI/ITRE/TRAN, and energy/transport attachés in Member State representations; Knowledge of key dossiers: Strong working knowledge of the Fit for 55 framework, including RED, ETS, FuelEU Maritime, ReFuelEU Aviation, and fleet CO₂ targets. Skills Technical knowledge on biofuels: ability to translate complex technical feedstock definitions, sustainability criteria, and GHG savings metrics into clear written and verbal political messages and statutory amendments; Autonomy: capable of delivering fast-turnaround advocacy materials during intense legislative negotiation phases; Languages: complete professional proficiency in written and spoken English is mandatory; additional EU languages (e.g., French, German) are preferred. Your role: The successful candidate is expected to contribute to BEUC’s enforcement and advocacy work , especially in the areas related to the implementation of the Digital Markets Act , by bringing behavioural insights - including coordinating data analysis on consumer behaviour and market practices - to BEUC’s work to better understand how consumers’ decision-making processes affect the effectiveness of regulatory interventions. The tasks will include, inter alia: Supporting BEUC's policy and enforcement teams by providing behavioural evidence and analysis in support of advocacy, litigation, complaints, and other regulatory discussions; Analysing consumer behaviour and decision-making in areas such as digital services, e-commerce, sustainability, financial services, and consumer rights; Contributing to the design and implementation of behavioural research projects , including experiments, surveys, field studies, and consumer testing; Translating research findings into clear policy recommendations and practical insights; Managing relationships with external stakeholders (e.g., research institutes, consultants, academic partners); Presenting findings to colleagues, consumer organisations, policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders; Monitoring developments in behavioural science relevant to consumer policy and market regulation; Contributing to publications, reports, position papers, and presentations. Your profile: Master's degree or PhD in behavioural economics, behavioural science, psychology, economics, data science, or a related field; Strong analytical skills and experience conducting behavioural research using quantitative and/or experimental methods; Strong interest in consumer policy , market regulation, and public-interest work; Ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-specialist audiences; Excellent drafting skills in English (an additional language is an asset); Ability to manage projects independently and work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams. item.description: Senior Policy Analyst OECD - Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development Paris, France From € 9783 per month Job Description Main Responsibilities Management and strategic leadership Help to lead and manage the Secretariat support to the Participants to the Arrangement, ensuring the effective delivery of their work programme and the implementation of decisions adopted by Participants. Direct the preparation of policy, analytical and decision-making materials for meetings of the Participants, ensuring high-quality outputs and timely delivery. Facilitate and support negotiations among Participants on technical and policy matters, helping build consensus and advance agreed outcomes. Oversee the Secretariat's internal and external communications activities, including briefing materials, speeches, stakeholder engagement and strategic messaging. Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of analysts, consultants and support staff by setting objectives, allocating resources, providing guidance and coaching, and managing performance. Technical and Policy Leadership Direct activities relating to the Technical Experts of the Participants ensuring effective preparation of meetings, high-quality documentation and follow-up of outcomes. Help to lead analytical and policy work on interest rate and premium disciplines for officially supported export credits, ensuring that evolving market developments, risks and member priorities are adequately reflected in policy discussions and negotiations. Help to lead work relating to aid and export credits, developing analytical assessments and policy recommendations to support the work programme of the Committees on Export Credits. Ensure the quality, consistency and relevance of analytical outputs, providing strategic guidance on complex technical and policy issues and promoting evidence-based decision making. Liaison, outreach and communication Co-lead the organisation of stakeholder consultations of the Working Party on Export Credits and Credit Guarantees (ECG) and the Participants to the Arrangement, including the Export Credits Forum, a major international event bringing together governments, export credit agencies, financial institutions, businesses and civil society organisations. Build and maintain effective relationships with member country representatives, export credit agencies, international organisations, private sector stakeholders and civil society organisations. Represent the Division in international meetings, conferences and stakeholder engagements, promoting OECD work and facilitating dialogue on export credit policy issues. Actively contribute to the communication of outputs on export credits issues, in relation with the communication unit. Participate in providing strategic advice and briefing materials to senior management, including the Head of Division, Director and national delegations, on policy developments, negotiations and emerging issues affecting official export credits. Qualifications Ideal Candidate Profile The successful candidate will combine strong policy judgment, analytical expertise and leadership skills with substantial experience in the field of officially supported export credits. They will demonstrate the ability to manage complex policy issues, lead multidisciplinary teams, build consensus among diverse stakeholders, and deliver results in a fast-paced international environment. Excellent interpersonal, communication and organisational skills, together with a strong capacity to work across cultures and disciplines, are essential. Academic Background Advanced university degree in economics, finance, public policy, statistics, or another relevant discipline. Professional Background At least eight years of progressively responsible experience in policy analysis, economic analysis or related fields acquired in a government administration, international organisation, financial institution, export credit agency, or research environment. At least five years of professional experience in the field of officially supported export credits. A strong knowledge of the OECD Arrangement on Officially Supported Export Credits and its associated Sector Understandings is essential. Proven experience supporting, facilitating or leading international policy discussions and negotiations involving multiple stakeholders and competing interests. Demonstrated experience managing and developing teams, including setting strategic objectives, allocating resources, coaching staff and overseeing performance. Sound project management experience, including the delivery of complex analytical workstreams involving extensive quantitative and qualitative data analysis. Strong record of producing high-quality analytical and policy-oriented work, including drafting reports, briefing materials and decision-making documents for senior audiences. Experience presenting complex policy and technical issues to senior government officials, international delegates and other high-level stakeholders. Tools Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, including experience working with large datasets and quantitative analysis. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 3); Enable People (Level 2); Ethics and Integrity (Level 2); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 3); Achieve Results (Level 3); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 3). There are three possible levels for each competency. The level for each competency is determined according to the specific needs of each job role and its associated grade. Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. item.description: Policy Analyst on Gender Equality (6-month-long Determinate Contract Aimed at Continuation with Indeterminate Contract) FEPS - Foundation for European Progressive Studies Brussels, Belgium € 4.500 per month gross Deadline for Applications: Monday, November 23 rd 2026 noon CET The Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS – www.feps-europe.eu ) is currently looking for one Policy Analyst for a thematic field: Gender Equality . The successful candidate is to join the FEPS Team based in Brussels from January 2027 onwards (cf. selection timetable below). FEPS is an equal opportunity employer, committed to enhancing fairness and to achieving workplace diversity. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all suitably qualified candidates, irrespective of gender, disability, marital or parental status, racial, ethnic or social origin, colour, religion, belief, or sexual orientation. About FEPS: The Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) is the think tank of the progressive political family at the EU level. Our mission is to develop innovative research, policy advice, training and debates to inspire and inform socialist and social democratic politics and policies across Europe. FEPS operates as hub for thinking to facilitate the emergence of progressive answers to the challenges that Europe faces today. FEPS works in close partnership with its members and partners, forging connections and boosting coherence among stakeholders from the world of politics, academia and civil society at local, regional, national, European and global levels. Today FEPS benefits from a network of 76 member organisations. Among these, 40 are full members, 31 have observer status and 5 are ex-officio members. In addition to this network of organisations that are active in the promotion of progressive values, FEPS also has an extensive network of partners, including renowned universities, scholars, policymakers and activists. FEPS’ ambition is to undertake intellectual reflection for the benefit of the progressive movement, and to promote the founding principles of the EU – freedom, equality, solidarity, democracy, respect of human rights, fundamental freedoms, human dignity, and the rule of law. Reporting Line: FEPS’ Policy Analysts report daily to the delegate of the Secretary General (i.e. the Director or Head of Programme appointed to supervise the thematic field in question). Mission of the Role: The mission of the Policy Analyst is to substantiate FEPS’ work on Gender Equality. S.he will embody FEPS’ internal expertise in the field (including feminism, anti-discrimination policies, equal opportunity, social investment, demography etc.). To do so, the Policy Analyst will design, steer and implement a coherent portfolio of FEPS (co-)funded projects (including its development and consolidation) aimed at impacting policies, political debates and/or public awareness related to the EU’s approach to Gender Equality. The ideal candidate will have the following profile: At least an MA or MSc degree in a relevant field. A PhD will be considered a relevant asset and account to the years of professional experience; Knowledge and interest for EU affairs and political sensitivity; At least 5 years professional experience in a field connected to Gender Equality; Proven expertise in quantitative and qualitative research, data analyses and surveys design; Capacity to follow developments at international, European, national, regional and local levels, and analyse relevant trends across political, economic and social dimensions; Experience in designing, overseeing and managing multi-stakeholders’ projects; Written and oral proficiency in English and in a second European language. Any additional European language will be considered an asset; Proven ability to draft analysis, research and policy recommendations; A strong set of soft skills, with specific reference to: Innovative and out-of-the-box thinking; High organisational and time-management skills; Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; Advanced interpersonal and social skills; Exceptional team player with the ability to contribute positively to a team; Ability to work under pressure and tight deadlines. Readiness to travel and adapt to flexible working hours. Employment conditions: The position is to be filled out as from January 2027 onwards. The position is to be filled out January 2027; The duration of the contract will be 6 months (potentially renewable in the form of an indeterminate contract); The fixed starting monthly gross salary will be 4.500 EUR; The workplace will be Brussels (Belgium); Applicants must be able to work and reside in Belgium; As FEPS is registered in Belgium, the contract will be under Belgian law. Applications’ composition and deadline: Applications are to be done online by Monday the 23 rd of November 2026 at noon CET . Your application is to include: A cover letter outlining your motivation for the post and your understanding of progressive values (maximum 2 pages); A detailed CV without picture (possibly in Europass format); A sample of work authored in the thematic field covered by the present notice (links or attached); The name of 2 referees with the related contact details. Applications not respecting the completion and submission instructions will not be considered. Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage for the purpose of applying with FEPS: Although specifically drafted for the purpose of research and writing activities, FEPS’ general approach and principles for the usage of Artificial Intelligence apply: https://feps-europe.eu/responsible-use-of-ai-in-research-and-writing-activities/ : Applicants wishing to use AI for the purpose of preparing their application are free to do so. Submitted MD file(s) will be used for the purpose of crosschecking (1) consistency with FEPS’ AI approach and principles and (2) the applicant’s AI literacy. Please note that the usage of AI is hereby not encouraged. The fact of using AI or not is not an assessment criteria as such. Transparency about its usage is and, in the case of usage, AI literacy will be. The tentative selection timetable is the following: Deadline for submission of complete applications: Monday 23.11.2026 noon CET ; Eligibility check and first assessment of written applications: This will result in a shortlist of no more than 6 candidates who will be invited for the subsequent step. First round of interviews of candidates & short written test between 30.11.2026 and 04.12.2026: This will result in a shortlist of no more than 3 candidates who will be invited for the subsequent step. Second interview of shortlisted candidates: early January 2027; Communication of the final results to candidates: by the end of January 2027. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Corporate-Services/1374174355/ . 4. Environmental and Social Sustainability and Climate Change A project’s environmental and social effects matter to a financing decision. In the Environmental and Social Sustainability Unit, you’ll help examine those effects and the climate risks and opportunities that come with them. The work includes screening risks, reviewing borrower information and legislation, and contributing to safeguards assessments. You’ll also support climate assessments covering Paris Agreement alignment and opportunities for adaptation or mitigation. Working through these questions with technical specialists offers a practical introduction to project due diligence and the methods behind it. Your profile: Studies in social studies, political sciences, community development, planning, applied economics, environmental sciences or a related discipline. Strong analysis and clear technical writing are essential, together with teamwork and the ability to manage changing deadlines. Courses on climate risks and resilience are an asset. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Environmental-and-Social-Sustainability-Climate-Change/1374177755/ . 5. Evaluation What did a development project achieve, and what could the next one do better? In the Office of Independent Evaluation, you’ll help gather and examine the evidence behind its findings. Expect to work with project and sector literature, analyse information, contribute to stakeholder interviews and prepare charts for evaluation outputs. You’ll also help with meetings and knowledge-sharing events. These assignments offer practice in research and presenting evidence, while showing you how independent evaluation informs learning and accountability. Your profile: Studies in evaluation, development studies, economics, social or political sciences, urban or environmental studies, business administration and international affairs. You should be interested in social, economic and environmental issues and highly proficient in MS Office, including Excel and PowerPoint. Knowledge of evaluation methods, additional analysis software and relevant professional or voluntary experience are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Evaluation/1374174555/ . 6. Legal Administrative Issues Staff rules, procurement and institutional privileges all raise legal questions for an international organisation. In the Office of the General Counsel’s Administrative Issues Unit, you’ll see how those questions are handled, working under experienced legal colleagues. You may assist with research on staff rules and disputes, privileges and immunities, or service contracts and procurement. Other assignments can include presentations and knowledge tools, including AI solutions for corporate contract management. It’s an opportunity to apply legal research and drafting to institutional matters with supervision. Your profile: Studies in law, focused on International Administrative Law, Law of International Organisations, or International or European Law. You’ll need accurate legal analysis, advising and drafting skills, the ability to manage deadlines and sound knowledge of IT and electronic document management tools. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Administrative-Issues/1374174855/ . 7. Long Term Investments and Liquidity If you enjoy finding meaning in financial data, this role offers a way to put that interest to work. You’ll be based in the Treasury & Asset and Liability Management Division, collaborating with colleagues in the CEB’s Dealing Room. Historical data analysis, capital markets notes and internal financial reports are all part of the work. You’ll also help develop dashboards covering financial and environmental, social and governance factors. It’s a practical setting for your data and coding skills, with exposure to treasury activities at a development bank. Your profile: Studies in finance, engineering, statistical and actuarial sciences, mathematics, banking or a related field. Strong analysis and critical thinking are important, supported by strong computer skills, particularly Excel including VBA coding or other coding languages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Long-Term-Investments-%26-Liquidity/1374177555/ . 8. Market Risk Risk models need calculations that stand up to scrutiny. In the Market Risk and Capital Management Unit, you’ll work on quantitative questions with colleagues across Risk & Control, Finance and IT. Assignments include developing checks for derivatives pricing curves and an in-house Credit Valuation Adjustment tool. You’ll analyse capital, provisioning and liquidity stress-testing models, and explore AI for model analysis, documentation and automation. You’ll get practice testing models and explaining what the findings mean. Your profile: Studies in quantitative finance, financial or applied mathematics, statistics, data science, computer science, engineering or an equivalent quantitative discipline. It requires strong quantitative and problem-solving skills, very good knowledge of at least one programming language, preferably Python or R, and an interest in risk modelling. VBA, SQL, Git or AI-assisted development tools are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Market-Risk-Stagiaire-Risque-de-March%C3%A9/1374189555/ . 9. You’ll support project identification and appraisal, help prepare Framework Loan Agreements and draft material for reports and presentation

Required profile A master’s degree in a relevant field; An interest in EU research & innovation and education policy, with specific interest in science and technology fields; Previous experience in a similar role or eagerness to build on relevant academic or professional exposure is considered an advantage; Good interpersonal skills and collaborative mindset, with the ability to engage effectively with others and work as an integral part of a team; Strong analytical, writing and communication skills with willingness to learn and grow in a stimulating environment; Flexibility, good organisational skills, a keen eye for detail, and a problem-solving approach; Proficiency in IT tools, including Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel); familiarity with WordPress and e-mail marketing systems like Mailchimp is an asset; Excellent command of spoken and written English; Legal entitlement to work in the European Union. Our offer A dynamic, stimulating and international work environment in an engaged and multicultural team; Ample opportunities for learning and professional development, including network building in Brussels; A paid internship based in Brussels for 6 months, under a Belgian CIP contract (Convention d’Immersion Professionnelle); A range of additional benefits, including lunch vouchers and reimbursement of public transport. The role can include occasional travels in Europe. Application process Applications should include: a CV without photo; and a cover letter outlining your motivation to join our team. Please submit your application as one PDF file by 25 November 2026 to Sophie Viscido, Secretary General, EuroTech Universities Alliance, at recruitment@eurotech-universities.eu , with the subject line: EU R&I policy Trainee Application . The first round of interviews is expected to take place online on a rolling basis in the last two weeks of November. A second round of interviews for shortlisted candidates is planned for early December in Brussels. The successful candidate is expected to join our team as soon as possible in January – the exact starting date can be discussed. By submitting your application, you confirm that you have read and understood the data protection information provided by EuroTech. About the EuroTech Universities Alliance The EuroTech Universities Alliance is a strategic partnership of leading European universities of science and technology, established in 2011. Guided by its Strategy 2030 , the Alliance brings together scientists and experts from its member universities to advance collaboration in research, innovation, infrastructure and education. It aims to contribute to a tech-driven, sustainable and resilient Europe. EuroTech’s activities focus on fostering synergies across the Alliance, contributing to knowledge-based policymaking, and strengthening European ecosystems along value chains, across borders, and between sectors. This is a varied, hands-on role, where you’ll be responsible for: Communications and content - Writing press releases, web news and social media posts, managing EU website content and social channels and creating visual materials that engage audiences and support our campaigns; Media and stakeholder engagement - Building relationships with Brussels-based journalists and stakeholders, raising the profile of our EU work and keeping our media contacts database up to date; Coordination and events - Helping organise in-person and virtual events, and support effective collaboration between our EU office, HQ and colleagues in Member States; Administration and office support - Taking ownership of practical administrative, operational and office management tasks, using our systems and supporting specific projects as needed. About you To succeed as our EU Communications Officer , you’ll need strong experience of political communications in Brussels that supports change with governments or intergovernmental institutions, ideally alongside experience in the non-profit sector. You’ll enjoy adapting your message to different audiences, and have a genuine interest in farm animal welfare, food and environmental issues. You’ll need to be a thoughtful, collaborative colleague who treats people with dignity and respect, works sensitively across cultures and takes pride in high ethical standards. Comfortable working independently as well as with others, you’ll balance communications projects with practical office tasks and follow through on your commitments. Skills and experience you’ll need to bring as our EU Communications Officer: Fluent English, excellent written and verbal communication skills, a strong news sense, and experience creating effective communications materials for a range of audiences, particularly for the Brussels bubble; Strong organisational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to prioritise your workload, use your initiative and take responsibility for projects and operational tasks; Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and internet tools, plus experience with, or a willingness to learn, Canva, InDesign, Photoshop and Adobe Premiere Pro; Previous experience with Brussels media or institutions, journalist contacts, campaigning knowledge and insight into EU political processes is essential. Event or webinar coordination, working in international teams, and additional European languages would be welcome. If you don’t meet every requirement but believe you could thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply. Why join us This is an opportunity to put your communications skills to work for a cause that matters, helping build a more compassionate future for farmed animals through our work in Brussels. You’ll get to collaborate with colleagues across our international organisation and contribute to campaigns connecting animal welfare with the future of food and farming. To support a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly ask that you do not include a photo in your CV. Please note that we may begin interviews on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged.
